topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of the lecture, focusing on the initiation and resolution of inflammation using previously introduced immune components.

topics.label: Innate Immune Recognition and Pattern Recognition Receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through conserved molecular patterns and pattern recognition receptor signaling systems.

topics.label: Inflammatory Mediator Release, Leukocyte Trafficking, and Systemic Impact
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how sentinel cell activation coordinates the recruitment of immune cells to tissues and can produce severe systemic complications such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Persistence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how inflammation is terminated and repaired, as well as the adaptations and consequences that occur when inflammation persists chronically.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the next lecture.
